content: Diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) programs, as endorsed by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), are highly beneficial for individuals with diabetes. However, significant barriers to accessing these programs persist across various levels, including the healthcare system, insurance payers, clinics, healthcare professionals, and patients themselves. At the health system level, logistical challenges such as limited clinic hours and inadequate transportation options can prevent patients from attending DSMES sessions. Administrative obstacles, such as restrictive referral pathways and insufficient reimbursement rates for DSMES services, further complicate access. Addressing these barriers requires a multifaceted and collaborative approach. Healthcare providers, policymakers, and community stakeholders must work together to improve the availability and utilization of DSMES programs. This may involve expanding clinic hours, improving transportation options, streamlining referral processes, and increasing reimbursement rates for DSMES services. Reimbursement for DSMES through Medicaid, Medicare, and other insurance programs plays a critical role in incentivizing participation. Enhanced reimbursement policies can make these services more accessible to patients, ultimately improving diabetes management outcomes.
